# BioTSR — method capability matrix

<!-- GENERATED by validation/scripts/capability_matrix.py from the
     method registry. Do not edit by hand: run the script instead. The test
     suite fails if this page and the registry disagree. -->

BioTSR is the unified software implementation of the Triangular Spatial
Relationship (TSR) methodology. This page lists every registered method and
what it supports, read directly from the package's method registry and its
table of target arguments. Each modifier cell is cross-checked against the
method's own validation: a "yes" is accepted, and a "—" is refused with
an error naming what the method does support. Every method runs under one
standard profile; there is no profile to choose.

**20 methods** — 2 calpha, 13 atomic, 5 cross.

## Standard profiles

* **`standard_calpha_selection_v1`** (`aa_selection`) — Standard aa_selection: the Ca atoms of an explicitly listed set of residues, labelled by residue identity in the residue label space at radix 30, 35-class Ca distance scheme, 29-class theta. Identical key space to ordinary protein Ca TSR -- only which residues take part differs, which is a SamplingProfile concern and not a KeySpace one.
* **`standard_protein_calpha_v1`** (`protein`) — Standard ordinary protein Ca TSR: math.pi, 35-class Ca distance scheme, 29-class theta, residue labels for the 20 regular amino acids and the supported modified residues (30 codes, radix 30), no mirror signing, no size filter. AA grouping swaps in the 23 grouped codes, also at radix 30. Structures are read by pdb_legacy, the one PDB reader BioTSR 1.0 ships; the reader affects parsing only, never key semantics, and is recorded in provenance.
* **`standard_aminoacid_type_v1`** (`aa_ind`, `aa_ind_mix`, `aa_ind_specific`) — Standard amino-acid selection by residue type or explicit residue identity (aa_ind / aa_ind_mix / aa_ind_specific): every admitted heavy atom of every matching residue, pooled into one calculation. 29 theta classes, 18 atomic distance classes, radix 112. Carries the family's exact-atom-count completeness rule (ADR-004), applied per residue instance. Standard-only: no historical implementation selects by type.
* **`standard_aminoacid_atom_selection_v1`** (`amino_acid_atom_selection`) — Standard pooled amino-acid atom selection: math.pi, the 18-class atomic distance scheme, 29-class theta, the 112-radix element labels. Uses WebsiteTSR's spec-correct element and altLoc admission and no completeness policy, as this method's historical implementation did.
* **`standard_aminoacid_atomic_v1`** (`amino_acid_atomic`) — Standard amino-acid atomic TSR: math.pi, the 18-class atomic distance scheme, 29-class theta, the 112-radix element labels, no mirror signing, no size filter. The completeness rule is this method's own historical exact-atom-count behaviour, which ADR-004 makes the standard for the methods that have one -- it is preserved, not relaxed. Atoms are admitted by the standard alternate-location rule shared by every method: blank or A kept, B and later excluded.
* **`standard_carbohydrate_v1`** (`carbohydrate`, `carbohydrate_atom_selection`) — Standard carbohydrate monomer/residue TSR: the HETATM heavy atoms of one carbohydrate residue identified by (carb_chain, carb_name, carb_id). Carries the historical exact-atom-count rule from expected_atom_counts.json, which is this scope's own historical behaviour (ADR-004).
* **`standard_carbohydrate_chain_v1`** (`carbohydrate_chain`) — Standard carbohydrate polymer/chain TSR: every admitted carbohydrate residue of one chain, pooled into one inter-residue calculation. NO completeness rule, because the historical polymer path explicitly passes apply_ligand_atom_count_filter=False -- a characterized fact, not an omission.
* **`standard_drug_v1`** (`drug`, `drug_atom_selection`) — Standard drug/ligand TSR: the HETATM heavy atoms of one ligand copy, identified by (drug_chain, drug_name, drug_id), all C(n,3) triangles. 29 theta classes, 18 atomic distance classes, radix 112. No completeness rule -- WebsiteTSR's ligand selector has none, and none is invented.
* **`standard_nucleotide_v1`** (`nucleotide`, `nucleotide_atom_selection`) — Standard nucleotide monomer/residue TSR: the ATOM heavy atoms of one nucleotide identified by (nt_chain, nt_name, nt_id), with the historical exact-atom-count table (G 23, A 22, C 20, U 20, DG 22, DA 21, DC 19, DT 20) preserved as this method's standard (ADR-004). Uses the spec-correct element and altLoc rules; the historical analyzer has no altLoc test at all, which is characterized separately.
* **`standard_nucleotide_chain_v1`** (`nucleotide_chain`) — Standard DNA/RNA chain TSR: every admitted nucleotide of one strand, pooled into one inter-nucleotide calculation. STANDARD-ONLY -- no historical implementation pools nucleotide residues. Each of the eight standard nucleotides takes part with every heavy atom it has, at a chain end or inside the chain; a nucleotide whose atoms differ from the standard set is named in a warning (ADR-114). No atom count is required and none is reconstructed.
* **`standard_atomic_cross_v1`** (`carbohydrate_protein_cross`, `drug_protein_cross`, `nucleotide_protein_cross`, `protein_protein_cross`) — Standard fully atomic cross TSR, shared by drug-protein, carbohydrate-protein, nucleotide/DNA/RNA-protein and atomic protein-protein cross: math.pi, 29 theta classes, the 18-class atomic distance scheme, the 112-radix element labels, the shared four-case ordering over integer labels, the midpoint median, no mirror signing, no size filter. Which points take part is a SamplingProfile concern: contact cutoff, side selectors and pool identity never enter this key space.
* **`standard_calpha_cross_v1`** (`protein_protein_calpha_cross`) — Standard Ca protein-protein cross: math.pi, 29 theta classes, the 35-class Ca distance scheme, the residue labels at radix 30, the shared four-case ordering, the midpoint median, float64. Identical key space to ordinary protein Ca TSR -- only which residues take part differs, and that is a SamplingProfile concern: interface residues are identified by ANY non-hydrogen atom pair within the cutoff and are then represented by their Ca, which itself need not be within the cutoff.

## Reading the table

* **vertices** — `Cα`: one point per residue, labelled by residue (the 20
  regular amino acids and eleven supported modified residues);
  `atomic`: one point per heavy atom, labelled by its element from the packaged element table.
* **cross** — triangles are drawn across two user-named sides, and every
  triangle has vertices on both.
* **AA grouping** — the grouped residue labels (23 codes, radix 30). Defined only over
  amino-acid labels, so only Cα methods offer it.
* **mirror** — negate a key whose pre-fold angle exceeds 90°. Off by default.
* **size filter** — keep triangles whose longest edge is below a cutoff. Off by
  default.
* **SSE** — the 18 secondary-structure categories. An annotation: it changes no
  key and neither identity fingerprint.
* **target arguments** — the arguments that say *what* to compute on, beyond
  the chain; **bold** ones are required. Python takes them as keyword
  arguments (`residue_types=`), the command line as flags with dashes
  (`--residue-types`). An argument a method does not read is refused by
  name rather than ignored.
* **standard profile** — the fixed conventions (distance and angle schemes,
  label scheme, admission rules) a method runs under. Modifiers vary a run;
  the profile itself cannot be replaced.

Candidate-strategy extensions (for example CA-kNN) are not part of BioTSR 1.0
and are absent from the registry.
